<!-- The numbers, figures and tables in the paper are made here, not in the
     manuscript. octavo build watches the .qmd and runs quarto render when needed. -->

<!-- octavo:example This .qmd is the template octavo init wrote, and right now
     it makes up **fake data** on the spot. Once it reads your real data, delete
     the `octavo:example` marks with it. While any mark is left, octavo check
     reports it as a template leftover. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Load octavo.R from this same analysis/ folder. When octavo build runs this,
# OCTAVO_ROOT is set, so it is found wherever it runs from.
root <- Sys.getenv("OCTAVO_ROOT", unset = "")
source(if (nzchar(root)) file.path(root, "analysis", "octavo.R") else "octavo.R")
```

## Data

```{r}
#| label: data
# Reading real data (raw data in data/raw/, cleaned data in data/derived/):
#   d <- read.csv(file.path(ov_root(), "data", "derived", "analysis.csv"))
# Clean it in a .qmd too, writing the result to data/derived/. Never modify data/raw/.
#   raw <- read.csv(file.path(ov_root(), "data", "raw", "survey2024.csv"))
#   d <- subset(raw, !is.na(x))
#   write.csv(d, file.path(ov_root(), "data", "derived", "analysis.csv"),
#             row.names = FALSE)

# octavo:example start — fake data. Replace with code that reads yours, then delete
set.seed(20260101)
d <- data.frame(
  x = rnorm(1523, 12, 3),
  y   = rnorm(1523, 50, 10)
)
d$y <- d$y + 0.34 * d$x
# octavo:example end

ov_value("n_obs", nrow(d), note = "observations used in the analysis")
```

## Estimation

```{r}
#| label: model
m <- lm(y ~ x, data = d)
s <- summary(m)$coefficients

ov_value("coef_x", s["x", "Estimate"])
ov_value("se_x",   s["x", "Std. Error"])
ov_value("p_x",    ov_pval(s["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]))
```

Write `{{n_obs}}` `{{coef_x}}` `{{p_x}}` in the manuscript and these values go in.

## Figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-trend
p <- function() {
  plot(d$x, d$y, pch = 16, col = "#4477aa55",
       xlab = "x", ylab = "y")
  abline(m, lwd = 2)
}
ov_figure(p, "trend")      # figures/trend.pdf and .png
```

In the manuscript, write `![Trend](../../figures/trend.png){#fig-trend}` and
refer to it as `@fig-trend` (it is numbered when typeset: Figure 2.1).

## Table

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
tab <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("x", "y"),
  Mean = c(mean(d$x), mean(d$y)),
  SD = c(sd(d$x), sd(d$y))
)
ov_table(tab, "summary",
         notes = paste0("Note: N = ", nrow(d), "."))
```

This writes the table's contents (tables/summary.typ / .tex / .md). In the
manuscript, the one line `: Descriptive statistics {#tbl-summary}` puts it
there with its caption, and `@tbl-summary` refers to it.
